pages.note: Published CLI under test is extension@4.1.3. Verified the --browser choice list against `extension dev/build/preview/start --help`, ran `build --browser=all` (expanded to chrome+edge+firefox exactly as claimed), ran `build --browser=chromium,chromium-based,gecko-based` (engine targets built with no binary and got their own dist/<target>), confirmed dist/chrome and dist/chromium are byte-identical via `diff -r`, confirmed `install all --where` lists chromium, and confirmed EXTENSION_PREFER_CHROMIUM_SNAPSHOT plus the four provenance labels exist in the shipped CLI. Fallback-at-launch and named-fork auto-location claims need a real browser launch, so they were left unverified.

Ran --help for every command in the chooser and checked each example's flags exist (publish --ttl, logs --follow/--context, inspect --tab/--with-console, eval --context, storage get --key, reload --context, open <surface>, doctor --browser, capabilities). Confirmed bare `extension` exits 0 and prints full help, `--template=new-react` is a real catalog name, and `telemetry` accepts enable/disable/status. All 16 internal doc links resolve to existing files.

Confirmed Chromium routes background to service_worker and Firefox to scripts from one source (built both, compared emitted manifests) and that per-browser dist/<browser> artifacts are emitted. The `type: "module"` auto-set claim failed an explicit build test with an ESM background entry.

Checked every row of the load-blocker catalogue and the repair table against the shipped implementation in the installed package (extension/dist/browsers.cjs blocker functions and extension-develop sanitizeFatalManifestShapes). Commands cap of 4 suggested_key, minimum_chrome_version comparison against the resolved binary, _locales/default_locale/__MSG_ rules with @@ exemption and case-insensitive lookup, storage.managed_schema, and all eight repairs (including the `{}` empty default_icon form) match exactly.

Built a project twice with an extension.config.js using first the object-merge `config: { resolve: { alias } }` form and then the `config: (config) => config` function-hook form; both resolved a custom @ui alias into the bundle. Confirmed the CLI looks for extension.config.js/.mjs/.cjs, that @rspack/core is the bundler, and that `browser` and `commands` are real first-class config keys in the shipped config-types.d.ts.

Scaffolded `create ts-check --template=typescript` with the published CLI and listed the result: the template ships sidebar/, content/, and background.ts, with no popup anywhere. The GitHub source link resolves to a real examples directory; the screenshot path resolves but points at a different template.

Mostly platform-behavior prose about MV3 service workers and dynamic import(), which cannot be checked without a browser. The checkable parts (four internal cross-references) all resolve to existing pages, and no framework-specific claim is made that contradicts observed CLI behavior.

Verified the five command-chooser examples against --help, that --template=new-react is a real catalog name, that `--browser=chrome,firefox` is accepted, that all five internal links and the /images/BANNER.png asset exist, and that pnpx still resolves (aliases pnpm dlx on pnpm 10.33.0). The version-agnostic CLI-version Info box is correct: `extension --version` prints 4.1.3.

Built the official content-css-modules template source with the published 4.1.3 CLI. Content-script CSS modules do produce a JS class-name map, which contradicts the page's own 'Content script note'. All template names, the repo link, and the screenshot asset check out.

Confirmed new-vue and content-vue are real catalog names with existing screenshots and example directories. Built a Vue project with only `vue` installed: no auto-install and no restart prompt occurred, and the shipped optional-dependency resolver throws an install-hint error instead, contradicting the page's 'installs it and asks for a restart' claim.
Pure navigation index. Ran a link-resolution pass over all nine chooser targets plus the two next-step links; every one maps to an existing .mdx file in the repo. No behavioral claims to test.
